newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila 1996 debt payment ratio down to 11.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Manila 1996 debt payment ratio down to 11.6 pct.

text.p: The Philippines' debt payment ratio shrank to 11.6 percent last year and is expected to dip further to 10.6 percent in 1997, the Central Bank said on Sunday.

The 1996 figure represents the ratio of total debt payments of $5.1 billion, including $3.1 billion principal payments and interest payments of $2 billion, to exports of goods and services totalling about $44 billion for the year, the bank said in a news release.
The ratio rose to 38 percent in 1982 in the closing years of late president Ferdinand Marcos's rule when the Philippines was forced to seek a moratorium from international creditors, it said.

For 1997, the Philippines is expected to pay $3.4 billion in principal payments and $2.2 billion in interest payments, or a total of $5.6 billion, the bank said. It did not give figures of projected export earnings.
The country's foreign debt stood at $37.778 billion as of last December.
